research_problem: Mobile apps implement input validation client-side while backend web APIs fail to replicate it, enabling 'Web API Hijacking' (parameter tampering) attacks
technical_approach: WARDroid: FlowDroid backward (inverted) taint slicing from HTTP points of interest, augmented PDG with UI constraints and EdgeMiner callbacks, path constraints in Z3/Z3-Str, request templates; NoTamper-style per-disjunct negation to craft invalid requests; edit-distance response comparison against sanitized valid responses
primary_contribution: First systematic approach and framework for detecting mobile-to-web API validation inconsistencies; definition of Web API Hijacking
dataset_benchmark: 10,000 popular free Google Play apps (AndroZoo, top 10 categories); 1,000 flagged apps tested
evaluation_metrics: Flagged and verified app counts, unencrypted traffic counts, estimated victim population, single-app template count vs manual MITM
baselines: Manual MITM trace on one app only
key_findings: 4,562 of 10,000 apps flagged; 884/1,000 single invalid requests accepted (88.4%), 926/1,000 after more samples; 1,743 apps unencrypted; >6.47M potential victims; real exploits incl. zero-dollar checkout SDK, XSS via news comments, SQLi in money-transfer app, bank transfers to unconnected accounts
author_limitations: No obfuscated/native code, no state/token reasoning, no WebView JS, authentication needs manual credentials, false negatives not evaluated, response classifier only 'decent'
analyst_limitations: No measured precision; 'verified' means inconsistency not exploitability; server-at-least-as-strict assumption questionable; efficacy shown on one app; download sums as victims; no artifact; 2018 ecosystem; ethics of probing production servers without IRB
reproducibility: Low: no tool or app list released
suggested_extensions: Client-code-derived OpenAPI inference; three-way client/spec/server consistency checking; LLM-based analysis of obfuscated or WebView code; stateful authenticated hijacking with BOLA; learned acceptance oracle; post-2020 replication
evidence_location: Rules p.3; architecture p.5-8; response evaluation p.9; results p.9-10; case studies p.11-12; limitations p.12
integrity: Two-column order heavily scrambled; Tables I-III and Algorithm 1 partly lost; figures missing
